SAM11-01.note: f(5)=40, f(1)=0, (40-0)/4=10. Option 40 is f(5) and 8 is f(5)/5; both clean traps. Routine module-1 difficulty.

SAM11-02.note: L+2w=60, Lw=400 -> w^2-30w+200=0 -> w=10 (L=40) or w=20 (L=20). The 'parallel side is longer' clause is the ONLY thing killing w=20, and it does kill it (20 is not longer than 20). Exclusivity rests entirely on that one clause - if it is ever edited out the item has two defensible answers. Option 40 is L, 6.67 is 20/3 (equal-thirds misread). Stock fence-against-a-wall problem with the canonical 60m/400m2 constants. Upper-medium, not hard route.

SAM11-04.note: t=sqrt(x): t=2,3 -> x=4,9, both check in the original, sum 13. Option 5 is the sum of the t-values. Stock quadratic-in-form.

SAM11-05.note: f min = -4 at x=3; g max = 4+7 = 11. Option 4 is -f's max alone, 3 is the vertex x.

SAM11-06.note: (x-3)^2(x-r), constant -9r=18 -> r=-2, a=-(3+3-2)=-4, b=-3. Note option -3 is the value of b, so a solver who computes both constants and grabs the wrong one lands on a listed option - a good trap, not a defect. Genuine hard-route item.

SAM11-07.note: (3-x)/(3x(x-3)) = -1/(3x). This is the difference quotient of 1/x; a very stock complex-fraction item.

SAM11-08.note: 2^(2x+3x+6)=2^15 -> 5x=9 -> x=9/5. Key is written as the decimal 1.8 and 9/5 = 1.8 exactly, so no fraction/decimal mismatch here.

SAM11-09.note: xz=3y^2+1 -> y=sqrt((xz-1)/3); y>0 selects the positive root. All four options are the same object type, no options-only tell.

SAM11-10.note: a^2-3a-28=0 -> a=7 or -4; 'positive' kills -4. Option 4 is the smaller number, -4 the rejected root. Note the stem's word 'positive' eliminates one option from the option set alone - a single elimination, not a leak. Stock 'differ by 3 / squares sum 65' pair.

SAM11-11.note: Ratio of leading coefficients 6/2=3. SPEC CONCERN: end behaviour / horizontal asymptote of a rational function in this wording is not really on the Digital SAT Advanced Math spec; this reads precalc. Options -6 and 0 are weak enough that a blind solver is choosing between 2.5 and 3.

SAM11-13.note: p(1/2)=1/2+2-3/2+5=6; confirmed by actual polynomial division by 2x-1 (remainder 6). The non-monic divisor is the whole point and it is handled correctly - the remainder is p(1/2), NOT p(1/2)/2 or p(1/2)*2. Legitimately hard.

SAM11-14.note: 2x^3-x^2-25x-12. Option -12 is the constant term, -1 the x^2 coefficient, -21 a plausible slip. Same task as SAM11-03.

SAM11-15.note: (8+2w)(10+2w)=168 -> w^2+9w-22=0 -> w=2 (w=-11 rejected). Checked the alternate reading 'border area = 168': gives w=3.39, not a listed option, so no second defensible answer. Option 11 is |negative root|. Stock 8x10-photo-with-border problem with the canonical 168.

SAM11-16.note: Vertex x=5 lies OUTSIDE [0,3]; f is decreasing there, so least value is f(3)=-3. Option -7 is the unrestricted vertex value f(5) - the trap the item is built on, and the best-constructed item in the batch. Mild spec concern: closed-interval extrema is more precalc than DSAT, but it is reachable with SAT-level reasoning.

SAM11-17.note: Vertex p=20, R=800. Option 20 is the price. Stock revenue-parabola item.

SAM11-18.note: Zeros 3/2, 3, -4; sum = 1/2. THIS IS THE FRACTION/DECIMAL ITEM: the natural written form of the key is 1/2 and the listed option is '0.5'. They are the same number, so the option set is sound - but if the explanation still writes '1/2' this is exactly the mismatch the author reported fixing. Verify the explanation string, not just the option.

SAM11-19.note: f(2)=f(6) puts the axis at x=4, so f(7)=f(1)=0 by symmetry; solving the 3x3 confirms f(x)=-x^2+8x-7, f(7)=0. Minor guessability: the key value 0 is quoted verbatim in the stem as f(1), so a solver who spots only the symmetry and not the arithmetic still wins - that is legitimate reasoning, but it makes the item cheaper than its algebra suggests.

SAM11-20.note: 16^(3/4)=8, x^8->x^6, y^-4 -> y^-3. The four options are a clean 2x2 of (2 vs 8) x (y^3 vs 1/y^3); no tell.

SAM11-21.note: 240/n - 240/(n+4) = 2 -> n^2+4n-480=0 -> n=20 (n=-24 rejected). Option 24 is n+4, 12 and 10 are share values. Genuinely multi-step. Stock cost-sharing problem with the canonical $240 / 4 more / $2 less constants - of everything here this is the set-up most likely to collide with something already in the bank.

SAM11-22.note: 3g(x)-4=6x^2+5 -> g(x)=2x^2+3. Option 2x^2+1/3 is the forgot-to-divide-the-constant slip, 18x^2+19 applies f instead of f-inverse.

SAM11-23.note: sqrt(x+7)=1+sqrt(x) -> 6=2sqrt(x) -> x=9; checks (4-3=1). No extraneous root to reject, which makes it easier than it looks. Stock radical equation.

SAM11-24.note: k^2-100>0 -> k>10 for positive k -> least positive integer 11. Option 10 is the boundary (discriminant 0, ONE solution) and is the entire trap. Parameter-plus-discriminant is real module-2 material.
